request.state: A draft application lets an employee complete a limited business objective with model assistance. Owner-defined task edits already have schemas and enforce team membership, active workplace eligibility and current record versions; the owner's completion operation also rejects finished tasks. An operation-reference feature currently binds all record arguments, but ordinary scalar/structured inputs must still be supplied at invocation, and external model strings are not operation references. The language already has asynchronous typed sends with durable receipts, immutable business records, viewer-filtered queries and local calls using the human caller's actual privileges. Official model-tool examples return a selected function name and argument object for the host to process; structured output does not remove validation. Required behavior is one proposal per bounded turn, retained authorized input evidence, a full exact preview and explicit worker approval, fresh access/context/version checks, recoverable rejection, persistent reconnect and a stop flag that prevents later application. A model must never acquire arbitrary dispatch, execute code, invent accounts or reference undisclosed records. These contracts have no deployed compatibility requirement. Evaluate both application repetition and new shared semantics; there are no comparative measurements.

representation.instructions: What boundary should carry the frozen suggested operation through human confirmation?

criteria.explicit: Author separate typed proposal variants from each selected owner's inputs, retain the expected versions in the app and invoke a literal owner operation in each approved branch. This uses current constructs and exposes each policy step. The company must maintain duplicated argument descriptions and branches as the owner interfaces evolve.
criteria.invocation: Introduce a closed invocation type parameterized by existing owner operations. It stores all canonicalized inputs and expected reference revisions; provider-created values are validated using only the original authorized input references, and an ordinary local call consumes the approved value with current human authority. The application retains its own review and bounded-run decisions. Schema and branch duplication falls, in exchange for specifying a new value's validation, provenance and exact display/execution rules.
criteria.toolset: Make the operation allowlist a named declaration that derives a planning service and proposed-call schema, plus common persistence of context/proposal/approval identities. Explicit app policy controls confirmation, resource ceilings and current caller checks. More repeated coordination can disappear, but the generated lifecycle covers a larger semantic surface and must expose rejection, stale context and cancellation behavior.
